title: Jobs report day, 162k vs 55k: my 70 paper bots closed 547 trades and lost $1,819. The freeze is still off.
author: QuanTradin
selftext:
Jobs report came in at 162k against 55k expected, the Dow gave up 263 and futures moved to a 58% chance of a hike. I run paper desks on my own platform, so here is what 70 bots actually did with that.

Desk 2 (44 bots, mostly 1-minute rules): 546 trades closed, 276 winners, down $1,827 on the day. Worst three trades were all about $115 and all on SOXL or SOXS. Leveraged semis on a data day, no surprise.

Desk 1 (26 bots, daily and options): closed exactly one trade. Plus $8.

The honest bit: my first thought at the close was to let the agent that manages desk 2 loosen up and trade the evening session back. The desk has a freeze switch built for exactly that moment. The agent can read it. Only a logged-in human can flip it. I have never once flipped it, and neither has anyone else, on any desk.

Numbers are all paper. I built this, so weigh accordingly.

Did anyone's bot sit out today on purpose, or is that just something we say afterwards?

comments.author: Patient_Ant_5409
comments.body: I have a bot that follows an event calendar. And it doesn't operate until the events are consolidated. It also tracks news in real time. There are 2 layers before it starts trading.
